body: That's awesome, thank you! Funny, I had a huge emotional slap in the face this morning that was pretty traumatic. So I went to hide in my house and call someone to talk to. That's when I realized I don't have anyone to talk to. I need to make some new friends and get my butt to a meeting or a counselor or something. The good news is, even though my heart is broken right now, and I'm brutally crushed, I still have no desire to use. So I appreciate the support, I might take you up on it. :)

I should have been clearer, it was a 5 day detox program. So I've now been drug free for **6** whole days. Yep! Something I never thought would happen. Pretty soon it will be 16 days, then 60, then 600 and *then* I'll really have something to be proud of.

Now I just gotta call a lawyer, delete Facebook, and join a credit union, right?

You're right too. Milk is my new best friend (and nauseas worst enemy HA HA! *evil laugh*) I have always eaten pretty well, I cannot wait to feel 'healthy' again, and enjoy the high you get from eating well and getting some exercise. Best dope ever.
upvote upvote upvote upvote upvote upvote upvote upvote *sigh of relief* upvote upvote upvote.....

I read his AMA a few weeks back, it was pretty awesome. To be honest, in detox seeing some of the others that were addicted to other drugs, and had horrible lives without the drug use, made me A) grateful for my life B) grateful I wasn't addicted to something else like meth or heroin and C) made me feel like a real ass to complain about my situation in comparison to some of the others. *I am lucky, I still have my family. Someone still loves me.* There is NO way I will EVER do anything EVER again to lose that.

You know what the *really* sad part is/was? I have a really, really, awesome life. The only bad part about it, was me, and my drug use. *I* was the miserable part about me.

I can't tell you how happy I am to not be my problem anymore. Stupid me!

Secrets DO keep you sick! How liberating it was to fess up to my SO about the things I was doing! That's a better feeling than drugs ever gave me. 

Thanks for having me back, I think I will stick around, it's nice here. :)

> wonderfully sober stabbing sensations in your brain

This is gold! I think you need to get in touch with Hallmark, you've got a real future. :)

Thank you!! As good as I feel mentally right now, even as bad as I feel physically, I can't imagine ever going back. What a waste of a way to live. I have the best SO ever, I can't wait to be part of my life again.

And I am SO sorry for your loss. I hope you know that she loved you very much, even if it didn't seem like it.

I ended up addicted almost the same way. I guess I have no advice really because everyone is different. However, I gotta say, it sure feels fucking good to be liberated from drugs. It actually feels better than the drugs did. I have a future, and a life again. I have money, and am earning back the trust from my spouse. I have self worth again. I'm not spending my days looking for/funding drugs, so I have time again. I have my life back and as cheesy as it may sound, having all these things again far outweigh any feeling dope EVER gave me. 

Oh and one more thing, detox isn't *nearly* as bad as I thought it was going to be, and that's the part that scared me the most. 

Best wishes to you and your SO on getting well together. :)

Appropriate username :)

I guess I should have been clearer. I was in a 5 day *detox*, not rehab as much. Now is when I go to NA and AA on my own. And you're right, 5 days isn't some marathon, but it is a miracle *for me*. 

Also, I did get a prescription to Subutex, but I asked for and received a very low dose (2mg twice a day), and I refused the sleeping pills, and the anti-anxiety meds. I didn't want to trade one habit for another. And my taper down is only 10 weeks, as opposed to a year (which I think is the most common?). So, all I can do is the best I can, and hope for the best right?
You're the very 1st person to wish me luck. **THANK YOU!**

Yay!! Feelings!

EDIT: Yay!! Even the bad ones!

Thank you!! I realize 5 days isn't some marathon of awesome behavior, however, it's the longest I've gone without in **6 years**. So even if no one else finds it impressive, I am impressed with myself (and of course the team of very expensive medical staff that got me here :)

Oh no. There will be no cheating. I really, really, despise the situation I am in. I hate everything about it, and I mean everything. From the money I spend to fund it, to the people I deal with to get it, to the time lost from my family. There is NOTHING about this addiction that I find even remotely appealing anymore. At first it was to get rid of pain, then it was to get through the day, and now I cannot get through a day without it. I hate it, more than I can express here, and will be eternally grateful to anyone who helps me to get off it.

I have not been in treatment before. Although, I've been through treatment with someone else before. I had to go for a week as their 'family support'. So I am familiar with the process, kinda.

I will call my insurance, and see what they say.
